summary: 1. No new meeting notes this pass — the last 7 days' Notion query returns fifteen results, all already ingested. 2. 2. Sep 5 production: ore collapses to 279 BCM / 753.3 t against a 2,954.2 BCM target — a -90.6% miss, the sharpest ore shortfall of the fiscal cycle, worse than Sep 1's prior worst of -64.32%. 3. Only one block (745-145-1) produced any ore at all. 4. The single day's miss wipes out the entire MTD ore surplus, flipping the MTD ore line from +8.29% (Sep 4) to -0.69%. 5. Drilling misses target for the first time in five days (-1.8%), and no blast was recorded for a second straight day. 3. 6. Fleet: DT-108 opens a fourth distinct fault in two weeks (Brake Jam); DZ-279 newly down; DT-129 recovers a second time. 7. The Daily Availability report's full long-standing-down register is read in one place for the first time this pass, surfacing four units — DT-79, WL-101, LV-049, MACN-018 — all down since 1-Feb-26, 216 days each, plus LT-200 crossing 100 days down for the first time. 8. Abel Pienaar delivers the detailed Maaden action plan Ivan Anthony demanded, a day ahead of the Sunday (7-Sep) deadline. 9. It names specific KPI targets (excavator/truck availability >88%, drill >85%, unscheduled downtime -20%), attributes root causes to named units (EX-253, DT-108/109/346/347), confirms only one unmined August block remains (171-735RL), and reframes Stage 6 pushback as part of the recovery strategy — consistent with Ivan Anthony's own 4-Sep framing. It does not mention Outliers Mining Solutions, adding weight to the open question of whether that engagement has actually started. 5. Maaden's own mining engineer independently issues a written ROM Bin Communication and Escalation Plan, corroborating the 5-Sep crusher-feed meeting's verbal protocol with a formal sign-off template and naming the Plant Manager and JRAR Production Manager as jointly accountable. 6. A new document type appears in RAW for the first time: a JRAR-internal "Weekly Operational Review" deck (distinct from the Maaden bi-weekly plan deck). It flags its own 16,709 BCM broken-stock discrepancy against the client report and explicitly marks one of its own sections as unverified "carried forward" content. Four earlier same-morning revisions of the deck, plus two out-of-scope stray/generated-overwrite copies in a `_to_delete` subfolder, were registered but not separately opened. 7. Grade Control September 2026.xlsx now exists as two diverging copies (Production report/ and Grade Control & Stockpiles/) — previously byte-identical, only one was refreshed this pass. Daily Drill Sampling Record-2026.xlsx did not receive a Sept 5 tab and is now a day behind every sibling daily workbook. No new meeting notes. Important References folder re-checked: 37 files, no new content since the 105th/107th/108th passes' last check.
